A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Value-Spectrum and retain the same underlying research framework. All 19 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original VLM preference scores, persona-induction experiments, image-versus-text comparisons and human evaluation of screenshot representativeness.

after.justification: V3 reports revised preference results and retains original persona and modality experiments. It additionally reports cultural-distribution analysis and human validation of value labels.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces contextualized interest questions with explicit one-word liking judgments and like/dislike explanations, also reflected in Figure 12. Section 3 changes the stated retrieval distance from L2 to cosine. The overall CLIP retrieval framework and Simple/ISQ persona-induction mechanisms remain.

E1.justification: The 50,191-video corpus, three platforms, ten Schwartz values and PersonaChat coverage remain. Appendix G adds human judgments of screenshot and full-video agreement with assigned value labels, extending the earlier human task of judging screenshot representativeness. The cultural audit examines existing data rather than adding new cultural domains.

E2.justification: The main preference comparison expands from six to eight models: Gemini 1.5 Pro, Qwen-VL-Plus and CogVLM are replaced by Gemini 2.0 Flash, Qwen2.5-VL-Plus and CogVLM2; DeepSeek-VL2 and InternVL2 are added. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Blip-2 remain. The reported persona and modality comparisons retain their model sets.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes its elicitation prompts and reported retrieval-distance setting. New protocols include a 2,614-image caption-based cultural audit and a 500-pair, three-annotator value-validation study with sequential screenshot/video judgments and explicit handling of inaccessible videos. Five images per keyword and ten 100-scroll persona trials remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices F and G investigate cultural representation and whether retrieved screenshots and videos express their assigned Schwartz values. These substantially extend validation beyond v2's screenshot-representativeness and modality-sensitivity studies, which remain present.

E5.justification: V3 removes the entire per-model, per-value mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting from Table 1. Figure 7 retains dispersion across values, which does not replace the removed within-value variability information. The ten-trial persona protocol remains, with no added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the main preference results under revised settings; for example, GPT-4o's Self-direction and Stimulation entries change from 96 and 90 to 78 and 56. Figure 6's leading values shift from Hedonism/Self-direction to Universalism/Benevolence. V3 adds cultural counts and 90.6% screenshot versus 87.6% video value-label agreement, while removing v2's keyword-level Tables 2–11. Persona and modality table values are retained.

T1.justification: The alignment-increase and ISQ scoring equations remain unchanged, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The retrieval-distance substitution is an operational metric choice without new mathematical derivation or formal properties.

C1.justification: The benchmark, dataset and persona-induction contributions remain. The introduction and conclusion revise the headline shared-value findings toward Universalism and Benevolence. The introduction also changes Claude's ISQ claim from largest gains to highest alignment, although the retained persona tables do not establish an overall Claude lead.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds a concrete cultural-applicability qualification: Western signals dominate, motivating targeted collection to improve balance. Appendix G interprets human agreement as support for retrieval and labeling validity and discusses inaccessible videos. V3 also removes v2's specific explanation connecting the Hedonism finding to societal pursuit of pleasure.

D1.justification: The access statement changes from an anonymous dataset-download link to a GitHub location described as providing complete code and data. Table 1 adds model-size and open-source metadata. Conversely, v3 no longer explicitly attributes keyword generation to GPT-4o, stating only that keywords are curated.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds foundational value-theory and psychometric references and explicitly positions the work against ValueNet, ValueBench and Yadav et al.'s multimodal cultural-value study. References for newly evaluated models are added, while Wrosch and Scheier's pleasure-related interpretation is removed. The broader related-work organization remains.

P1.justification: V3 edits grammar, tense, terminology, author/contact information and captions; rewrites portions of Sections 2.3 and 4.2; and reorders the contribution bullets. Appendix organization changes to accommodate the new analyses, but the main section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is transposed and gains metadata columns. Figure 5 changes from filled radar regions to lines with an expanded legend and percentage scale; Figures 6–7 are rescaled. Ten keyword tables are removed, cultural and human-validation tables are added, and Figure 12's example dialogues are revised. Retained appendix tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new human value-label validation addresses a substantive gap left by v2's screenshot-representativeness study, and the cultural audit makes the dataset's limitations clearer. These gains are tempered by lost keyword-level results and per-value standard deviations, incorrect non-Yes averages in Table 9, and the unsupported overall Claude alignment claim. The added validity evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial one.
